definitions: Around a valence-vvertex, label edge neighbors E_jand opposite face vertices F_jin cyclic order. A face point is F′_j=(P+E_j+F_j+E_(j+1))/4.
The edge rule is E′_j=(P+E_j+F′_(j−1)+F′_j)/4.

result.name: Exact nonconstant Fourier block
result.statement: For a nonzero modez=e^(2π ik/v), P=0, E_j=Ez^j, F_j=Fz^j, the block on(E, F)is M(z)=[[(3+c)/8,(1+z^(−1))/16],[(1+z)/4,1/4]], c=cos(2π k/v). Its eigenvalues are(5+c±√((c+9)(c+1)))/16.
result.proof: Substitute the modal values into the face rule to get F′=[(1+z)E+F]/4. In the edge rule, F′_(j−1)+F′_jcontributes(1+z^(−1))F′, so its E-coefficient is1/4+(2+z+z^(−1))/16=(3+c)/8and its F-coefficient is(1+z^(−1))/16. This proves the block. Its trace is(5+c)/8and determinant1/16. The quadratic formula gives the stated eigenvalues. Sincec∈[−1,1], the radicand(c+9)(c+1)is nonnegative; for this standard block the eigenvalues are real. Atz=−1the off-diagonal entries vanish and M=I/4, so the repeated eigenvalue there is semisimple.

example.setup: Takev=4, k=1, andv=6, k=1,2.
example.calculation: Forv=4, c=0, the eigenvalues are1/2and1/8. Forv=6, thek=1values are(11±√57)/32; thek=2values are(9±√17)/32. These exact formulas differ from the recovered ad hoc constants. Sixth roots of unity may put√3in matrix entries, but that does not force complex eigenvalues or a motivic interpretation.
example.conclusion: The spectrum now follows from explicit subdivision rules and a two-by-two characteristic polynomial.

entries.limits: This is the nonconstant one-ring block, not a complete proof of global surface regularity or every extended stencil. Different modified schemes can have different blocks and must supply their own rules.
entries.extension: Derive the constant-mode vertex block and characteristic map, then verify the eigenvalue ordering and regularity conditions required by a subdivision-smoothness theorem.

entries.summary: The retrieved dated file supplies an explicit S₆and a cube-zero nilpotent claim. The strictly upper-triangular part is indeed cube-zero, but it fails to commute with the diagonal. The actual Jordan–Chevalley nilpotent part is square-zero. Distinguishing these decompositions makes the finite algebra correct.

result.name: Exact commuting semisimple–nilpotent decomposition
result.statement: S=S_s+Nwith S_s=diag(B, B), N=[[0, I₂],[0,0]],[S_s, N]=0, N²=0, N≠0. Since Bhas distinct eigenvalues, S_sis diagonalizable, and S is similar to J₂(a)⊕J₂(b).

A two-by-two triangular matrix with distinct diagonal values is diagonalizable; explicitly T=[[1, r/(b−a)],[0,1]]satisfies BT=Tdiag(a, b). Conjugating Sbydiag(T, T)diagonalizes both Bblocks while leaving I₂unchanged. Reorder the basis to pair the twoa-coordinates and the twob-coordinates; the result is J₂(a)⊕J₂(b). This proves the commuting Jordan decomposition and its two block sizes. By contrast write S=D₀+Uwith D₀=diag(a, b, a, b)and Uits raw strict upper triangle. The raw Uhasexp(t U)=I+t U+t²U²/2, butexp(t S)cannot be replaced bye^(t D₀)e^(t U)because D₀and Udo not commute. A legitimate step-two unipotent example is E₁₂, E₂₃with central commutator E₁₃, where the finite Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff correction is explicit.

entries.status: Classical or newly chosen explicit model developed with proof; historical conjectures delimited
entries.summary: The recovered refinement narrative invoked the plastic constant and a Pisot–Frobenius archetype. The Padovan companion matrix provides a complete classical instance:one expanding real algebraic unit and two contracting conjugates. definitions: Letp(x)=x³−x−1andlet ψ be its positive real root.

result.name: Pisot property and asymptotic mode splitting
result.statement: ψ>1is the unique real root ofp, and its two other roots are complex conjugates of modulus ψ^(−1/2)<1. The companion matrix has characteristic polynomialp; generic solutions are A ψ^nplus an exponentially decaying oscillatory term.
result.proof: The polynomial discriminant is−4(−1)³−27(−1)²=−23<0, so it has one real root and a nonreal conjugate pair. Sincep(1)=−1andp(3/2)>0, the real root lies in(1,3/2). The product of all three roots is one, so ifz, overline zare the other roots, ψ|z|²=1, proving the modulus. The rational-root test excludes±1and shows irreducibility over Q, so ψ is an algebraic integer of degree three with all other conjugates inside the unit circle:a Pisot number. Expandingdet(t I−C)givesp(t); the roots are distinct, so diagonalization gives the three-mode recurrence solution. The real dominant coefficient Acan vanish for specially chosen initial data, but not for a positive Perron eigencomponent.

entries.title: Discrete Hodge splitting and the correct cohomology transport group
entries.status: Classical or newly chosen explicit model developed with proof; historical conjectures delimited
entries.summary: The recovered subdivision program used harmonic/curvature blocks and an SL(2g, Z)transport. A finite cochain complex has an exact Hodge decomposition, but an oriented surface’s integral intersection form restricts its cohomology transport more strongly than determinantone.
definitions: For finite inner-product cochain spaces with differentiald andd²=0, let Δ=d*d+dd*.
On an oriented genus-gsurface, the first integral cohomology carries a nondegenerate skew intersection matrix J.

result.name: Finite Hodge decomposition and symplectic necessity
result.statement: C^k=im d_(k−1)⊕ker Δ_k⊕im d_k*orthogonally, andker Δ_krepresents H^k. Any orientation-preserving surface-induced transport Msatisfies M^TJM=J, hence lies in Sp(2g, Z), not merely SL(2g, Z).
result.proof: The two image spaces are orthogonal because⟨du, d*v⟩=⟨d²u, v⟩=0. Also⟨x, Δ x⟩=||dx||²+||d*x||², so harmonic vectors are exactlykerd∩kerd*. The orthogonal complement of the two image spaces is precisely that intersection, proving the decomposition. Every cocycle is an exact part plus a harmonic part, and a harmonic exact vector has zero norm, so harmonic representatives are unique. For transport, the cup-product/intersection pairing is preserved by an orientation-preserving homeomorphism; writing this invariance in a basis gives M^TJM=J. In dimensiontwo this is equivalent todet M=1, but in higher dimensions it is stronger.

example.setup: For a three-edge cycle oriented consistently, take the incidence differentiald:C³→C³. Forg=2compare a determinant-one matrix with J=[[0, I₂],[−I₂,0]].
example.calculation: The harmonic edge space isspan(1,1,1), and its period is the sum of edge values. Let A=[[1,1],[0,1]]and M=diag(A, I₂). Then det M=1but M^TJM has upper-right block A^T≠I₂, so it is not symplectic and cannot represent the claimed oriented-surface transport.
example.conclusion: Harmonic degrees of freedom and allowed transport have exact finite definitions and an explicit obstruction.

entries.title: Cancelling quadratic drift requires an expansion, not a benchmark label
entries.status: Classical or newly chosen explicit model developed with proof; historical conjectures delimited
entries.summary: The recovered cohomological-correction discussion reported ε²to ε⁴improvement and an exact-rationalk=35validation. No underlying certificate was recovered. A standard extrapolation theorem shows a constructive mechanism with the exact assumptions and residual coefficient visible.
definitions: Suppose F(h)=F₀+c h²+d h⁴+R(h), with|R(h)|≤M h⁶for0<h≤h₀.
Define the corrected estimate G(h)=[4F(h/2)−F(h)]/3.

result.name: Explicit order-four extrapolation
result.statement: G(h)=F₀−d h⁴/4+R_G(h), where|R_G(h)|≤(17/48)M h⁶. Thus theh²term cancels exactly and the remaining leading drift is quartic when d≠0.
result.proof: Substitute the expansion into4F(h/2)−F(h). The constant coefficient is3F₀; the quadratic coefficient is4c(h²/4)−ch²=0; the quartic coefficient is4d(h⁴/16)−dh⁴=−3dh⁴/4. Dividing bythree gives the formula. The remainder obeys|R_G|≤[4M(h/2)⁶+Mh⁶]/3=(17/48)Mh⁶. This is a complete cancellation proof. It also identifies a necessary structural assumption:the samec, dand F₀must govern the two scales. If the correction changes the problem or if an oddh³term is present, the claimed quartic order does not follow.

example.setup: Take F(h)=7+3h²+5h⁴exactly, and compareh=1andh=1/2.
example.calculation: F(1)=15, F(1/2)=7+3/4+5/16=129/16. Hence G(1)=[4·129/16−15]/3=23/4=7−5/4. The uncorrected quadratic coefficient3has disappeared, and G(h)−7=−5h⁴/4for everyh. Every value is rational, so no floating-point ambiguity is involved.
example.conclusion: The improvement is a proved conditional approximation result with an exact example, rather than a claim inferred from a benchmark table.

entries.summary: The recovered RG framework usedt_i=μ_i⊙ΔΦ_iandrank Tas an intrinsic memory count. definitions: Let Tbe a matrix whose columns aret_i. Rank is the dimension of their linear span.

result.statement: rank(LTR)=rank Tfor invertible L, R. But transforming both μ and ΔΦ by the same invertible Ldoes not generally transform μ⊙ΔΦ by L, and can change its rank.

entries.title: The6.02dB identity refers to an amplitude ratio
entries.status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
entries.summary: The same physical ratio has different numerical logarithmic factors depending on whether one starts with power or amplitude. Coherent addition and independent addition are different hypotheses, with exact phase-dependent formulas.
definitions: For positive powers defineL=10log₁₀(P/P₀). IfP=cA² with fixed positivec, the same level difference is20log₁₀(A/A₀).
Two equal complex amplitudesA andAe^{iφ} sum coherently. Independent zero-mean signals with no cross covariance add their powers instead.
All logarithm arguments must be dimensionless ratios with the same reference convention.

result.name: Exact doubling and interference laws
result.statement: Doubling amplitude at fixed conversionc quadruples power and adds20log₁₀2≈6.02060dB. Doubling power adds10log₁₀2≈3.01030dB. Equal coherent amplitudes giveP_total/P_single=2+2cosφ.
result.proof: The amplitude-to-power law givesP₂/P₁=(A₂/A₁)², so ten times the logarithm of power becomes twenty times the amplitude logarithm. For coherent addition, |A+Ae^{iφ}|²=|A|²(2+e^{iφ}+e^{−iφ})=2|A|²(1+cosφ). Atφ=0 power is four times one signal; atφ=π it is zero. For independent or uncorrelated zero-mean signals, expectation of the cross term vanishes, leaving twice the single-signal power and the3.01dB result. These calculations identify exactly which statistical or phase assumption changes the reported gain.

example.setup: Compare phases zero,π/2 andπ for equal-amplitude inputs.
example.calculation: The power ratios are four,two and zero. The first gives6.02060dB, the second3.01030dB, and exact cancellation has no finite logarithmic level relative to positiveP₀. Rounding6.02 does not convert an amplitude statement into a universal gain for two devices or two noisy sources.
example.conclusion: The original identity is preserved with its mathematical domain and operational meaning made explicit.

entries.limits: Changing impedance or another amplitude-to-power conversion factor changes the simple20log formula. The result does not validate any proposed phonon, curvature or material-protection mechanism.
entries.extension: For unequal amplitudesA,B, deriveP=A²+B²+2ABcosφ and propagate a bounded phase error through it. The derivative−2ABsinφ shows where a phase-sensitive operating point is locally robust and where it is sensitive. Near destructive interference write φ=π+δ. Then P_total=2A²(1−cosδ)≤A²δ². The inequality 1−cosδ≤δ²/2 gives a global quadratic upper bound on leakage from a phase error, a stronger and more useful robustness statement than merely reporting the zero at perfect cancellation.

entries.title: A controlled gate is unitary but protection needs an error model
entries.status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
entries.summary: CNOT is an exact permutation unitary and creates an entangled state from a separable input. A telescoping estimate bounds accumulated implementation error, but unitarity alone does not prove fault tolerance.
definitions: DefineCNOT|a,b⟩=|a,b⊕a⟩ for binary labels. The Hadamard gate sends|0⟩ to(|0⟩+|1⟩)/√2.
For unitary gatesU₁,…,U_m and unitary approximationsV₁,…,V_m assume||V_j−U_j||≤ε_j in operator norm.
Protection is a statement about specified errors, encoding, correction and a performance bound, not merely a name for the intended gate.

result.name: Exact entangling gate and circuit error bound
result.statement: CNOT²=I andCNOT is unitary. CNOT(H⊗I)|00⟩=(|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2, whose one-qubit marginal isI/2. The two circuit products differ by at mostΣ_jε_j.
result.proof: CNOT permutes the four orthonormal basis states and is its own inverse, proving unitarity. Applying it to(|00⟩+|10⟩)/√2 gives the displayed Bell state. Taking a partial trace eliminates the two off-diagonal cross terms and leaves equal populations, so the pure joint state is not a product. For the error bound, subtractV_m⋯V₁−U_m⋯U₁ and insert mixed products one gate at a time. The resulting sum has termsV_m⋯V_{j+1}(V_j−U_j)U_{j−1}⋯U₁. Unitary factors have norm one, so submultiplicativity and the triangle inequality giveΣ ε_j. This is a worst-case coherent-error estimate and requires no stochastic independence.

example.setup: Take ten gates each with norm error at most10⁻³.
example.calculation: The final unitary error is at most10⁻². Acting on any normalized state gives state-vector error at most10⁻²; an expectation of an observable of norm one changes by at most2·10⁻². This bound does not imply a threshold theorem or a percentage of operational coherence.
example.conclusion: A correct gate and a protected implementation are separate mathematical claims with a calculable bridge only after errors are specified.

entries.limits: The calculation supplies no material implementation or hardware error rate. Fault-tolerant thresholds involve coding, locality, noise and repeated recovery assumptions absent from the recovered formulas.
entries.extension: Choose an explicit encoding and noise channel, verify the Knill–Laflamme conditions and compute a logical error bound after recovery. Compare it with the coherent telescoping bound before claiming protection.

entries.title: The oscillator connects a connection, a star product and an eigenstate
entries.status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
entries.summary: On the symplectic plane one can write the prequantum connection and verify its curvature directly. The constant-Poisson Moyal product and a normalized Gaussian then give exact, separately checkable quantization statements.
definitions: Use coordinates(q,p),ω=dq∧dp,H=(q²+p²)/2 andħ>0. DefineX_H byι_Xω=dH, givingX_H=p∂q−q∂p.
On the trivial complex line bundle set∇=d−(i/ħ)q dp. The formal Moyal product isf⋆g=f exp[(iħ/2)(←∂q→∂p−←∂p→∂q)]g.
The Schrödinger operator isĤ=−(ħ²/2)d²/dq²+q²/2 on an appropriateL² domain.

result.name: Exact curvature and quantization checks
result.statement: The connection has curvature−iω/ħ. The star commutatorq⋆p−p⋆q=iħ, andH⋆H=H²−ħ²/4. The Gaussianψ₀=(πħ)^−1/4exp(−q²/(2ħ)) is normalized and has energyħ/2.
result.proof: Because the connection one-form is scalar, its wedge square vanishes and∇²=d[−iq dp/ħ]=−i dq∧dp/ħ. Forq,p the bidifferential expansion stops after first derivatives, yieldingqp±iħ/2. ForH⋆H the first Poisson term is zero; the second derivative combination isH_qqH_pp+H_ppH_qq=2, so its coefficient is−ħ²/8 times two. Higher derivatives vanish. Differentiating the Gaussian givesψ₀″=(q²/ħ²−1/ħ)ψ₀, so substitution cancelsq² and leavesħψ₀/2. Its squared norm is one by the elementary Gaussian integral. Formal associativity of the Moyal product follows because the constant-coefficient operators on three tensor factors commute, making both parenthesizations the same exponential of the sum of pair operators.

example.setup: Setħ=1 and compare the classical fixed point with the Gaussian.
example.calculation: The classical point(q,p)=(0,0) hasH=0. The normalized quantum state has energy1/2 and variances〈q²〉=〈p²〉=1/2, givingΔqΔp=1/2. The difference is a quantified statement about a specified representation, not a change in the classical curvature formula.
example.conclusion: Each bridge has an explicit map or calculation and can be checked independently.

entries.limits: Prequantization alone does not choose a polarization or prove the full oscillator spectrum. The formal star product is not automatically a convergent product on every function space.
entries.extension: Construct the ladder operators, prove their commutator on Schwartz functions and derive all Gaussian–Hermite eigenstates. Then justify completeness and the self-adjoint operator domain rather than relying only on formal algebra. Since H is quadratic, every third derivative vanishes and its Moyal commutator with a polynomial equals iħ times the Poisson bracket exactly. In particular (q⋆H−H⋆q)/(iħ)=p and (p⋆H−H⋆p)/(iħ)=−q, reproducing the classical linear oscillator equations with no higher-order correction.

entries.status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
entries.summary: The plane contracts to its origin equivariantly, so its equivariant cohomology isH*(BS¹)=k[u]. Ordinary plane and free-loop-space cohomology are instead justk. These are different constructions with different retained symmetry data.
definitions: LetS¹ rotateC≅R². The Borel construction isES¹×_{S¹}C, and equivariant cohomology is its ordinary cohomology.

result.name: Complete equivariant calculation for the plane
result.statement: H*_{S¹}(C;k)≅k[u], with one generator in every nonnegative even degree and none in odd degree. H*(C;k)=H*(LC;k)=k in degree zero only.
result.proof: The homotopyr_s(z)=(1−s)z commutes with rotations and ends at the fixed origin. It descends to a deformation retraction ofES¹×_{S¹}C ontoES¹×_{S¹}{0}=BS¹. The standard cell decomposition ofCP∞ has one cell in every even dimension and no odd cells; its ring generatoru has nonzero powers, yieldingk[u]. For the ordinary loop space, contract every loop pointwise byr_s. This is a continuous contraction to the zero loop, giving the ordinary cohomology claim. entries.title: A nilpotent monodromy has a computable weight filtration
entries.status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
entries.summary: A two-dimensional unipotent matrix supplies an exact logarithm, a centered weight filtration and a compatible sl₂ representation. This concrete calculation isolates the linear algebra used in degeneration theory from an unprovided quantum enrichment.
definitions: Let V=Qe₁⊕Qe₂ and M=[[1,1],[0,1]]. Its nilpotent logarithm is N=logM=M−I because(M−I)²=0.
A monodromy weight filtration centered at one is increasing, satisfiesN(W_k)⊂W_{k−2}, and makesNʲ:Gr^W_{1+j}→Gr^W_{1−j} an isomorphism for every j≥0.

result.name: Explicit monodromy weight calculation
result.statement: The filtration isW_k=0 fork<0,W₀=W₁=Qe₁,W_k=V fork≥2. The mapN:Gr²_W→Gr⁰_W is an isomorphism. The nontriviality of this filtration does not alone define a limiting mixed Hodge structure.
result.proof: SinceNe₂=e₁ andNe₁=0, image and kernel ofN are bothQe₁. The proposed filtration is stable underN with the required two-step decrease. Both nonzero graded pieces are one-dimensional and the inducedN maps[e₂] to[e₁], proving the required isomorphism. Higher powers are zero and relate zero graded pieces. For an sl₂ triple setE=N,F=[[0,0],[1,0]],H=diag(1,−1). Multiplication gives[H,E]=2E,[H,F]=−2F,[E,F]=H. Weight index1−H assigns index zero toe₁ and two toe₂, agreeing with the filtration. This is the exact finite representation-theoretic content; a Hodge filtration, polarization and geometric degeneration are additional data. Over the integer lattice, replacing M by M_n=I+nN changes the coinvariants to Z⊕Z/nZ for n>0: the image is nZe₁. Tensoring with Q removes this torsion and leaves the same rational rank. This gives an explicit arithmetic distinction invisible to the real matrix rank alone.

example.calculation: Mⁿ=I+nN=[[1,n],[0,1]] for every integern. Invariants areQe₁; coinvariantsV/NV are generated by[e₂]. They each have dimension one, yet one is a subspace and the other a quotient. Confusing them would erase the nonzero connecting mapN.

entries.title: A kernel transform is an equivalence only when it has an inverse
entries.status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
entries.summary: On a two-point space the bounded derived category can be classified completely. Equivalences permute the two simple objects and shift them; a shift-and-swap gives an exact involution.
definitions: Letk be a field andD=Dᵇ(Vec_k×Vec_k), represented by pairs of bounded finite-dimensional complexes.
Write[1] for the cohomological shift. Each complex over a field is isomorphic in the derived category to the direct sum of its cohomology spaces placed in their degrees.
The simple objects areS₁=(k,0),S₂=(0,k). Their shifts are the indecomposable objects, and different simples have no morphisms in any degree.

result.name: Classification in a finite derived model
result.statement: Everyk-linear triangulated equivalence ofD permutesS₁,S₂ and assigns an integer shift to each. In particularF(V,W)=(W[1],V[−1]) is an equivalence withF²≅Id.
result.proof: Split every differential into its image, a complement in its kernel and a remaining complement; the image/complement pairs form contractible two-term summands. This leaves precisely the graded cohomology, proving the decomposition. An equivalence preserves indecomposability and all graded morphism spaces. It therefore sends eachS_i to a shifted simple. The two images cannot be shifts of the same simple, since then some shifted morphism between them would be nonzero although everyHom(S₁,S₂[n]) vanishes. Essential surjectivity forces both simple types to occur. Conversely a permutation with prescribed shifts has an inverse permutation with the opposite shifts and acts componentwise on morphisms, so it is an equivalence. For the displayedF, applying it twice cancels both shifts.

example.setup: TakeV=k in degree zero andW=k² in degree zero.

entries.title: Noncommutative observables still have identities and symmetries
entries.status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
entries.summary: Commuting self-adjoint matrices admit a common orthonormal eigenbasis. Noncommuting examples retain an identity and can have exact unitary symmetries; their uncertainty is a quantitative statement about a state.
definitions: An observable in this finite model is a self-adjoint complex matrix. Joint diagonalization means one unitary basis makes every matrix diagonal.
Use PauliX=[[0,1],[1,0]],Z=diag(1,−1),Y=[[0,−i],[i,0]], and identityI.
For normalizedψ, variance is(ΔA)²=||(A−〈A〉)ψ||². A symmetry may act by unitary conjugation.

result.name: Joint diagonalization and a sharp uncertainty example
result.statement: A finite commuting family of self-adjoint matrices is simultaneously unitarily diagonalizable. Forψ=(1,i)/√2,ΔX=ΔZ=1 and|〈[X,Z]〉|/2=1, attaining the Robertson lower bound.
result.proof: Diagonalize one self-adjoint matrix. Every matrix commuting with it preserves each eigenspace, becauseA(Bv)=B(Av)=λBv. Restrict the remaining self-adjoint matrices to those invariant eigenspaces and iterate; their orthonormal eigenbases combine into the required basis. Conversely diagonal matrices commute. For the inequality putu=(A−〈A〉)ψ andv=(B−〈B〉)ψ. Cauchy–Schwarz gives||u||||v||≥|Im〈u,v〉|=|〈[A,B]〉|/2. With the statedψ,〈X〉=〈Z〉=0,X²=Z²=I and[X,Z]=−2iY whileYψ=ψ. All claimed numbers follow directly. The same noncommutative algebra still containsI, andXZX=−Z is an exact conjugation symmetry.

example.setup: CompareI,Z withX,Z and evaluate their products on the chosen state.
example.calculation: I andZ share the standard basis. In contrastXZ=−ZX, so no common eigenbasis exists. NeverthelessI commutes with everything, each Pauli matrix is unitary, and conjugation byX exchanges the twoZ eigenstates. Noncommutativity therefore does not imply absence of identity, symmetry or algebraic consistency.
example.conclusion: The original contrast becomes a theorem about simultaneous diagonalization and state-dependent variance.

entries.limits: The finite result does not settle interpretations of quantum measurement or a Platonic ontology. Unbounded observables need common domains; zero commutator expectation in one state does not mean the operators commute.
entries.extension: For an explicit matrix algebra, compute its center and commutant. These identify classical sectors and exact symmetries without assuming that every noncommutative system has the same observable structure. The commutator expectation can vanish in a particular state even for noncommuting operators. For the maximally mixed qubit state I/2, both Pauli variances equal one but the commutator has trace zero. The displayed inequality is then valid but not sharp; operator commutation is stronger than one state’s expectation test.

entries.title: Closing a curve is distinct from choosing a polygon or a winding
entries.status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
entries.summary: A loop is a continuous map with equal endpoints; it need not be polygonal or noncontractible. A uniformly close polygonal approximation preserves winding whenever the straight-line interpolation avoids the reference point.
definitions: Letγ:[0,1]→C∖{0} be a closed piecewise smooth curve andd=min_t|γ(t)|>0.
Letp be a closed polygonal path withsup_t|p(t)−γ(t)|<d. Winding about zero is the integer degree ofγ/|γ|, or its logarithmic-derivative integral when smooth enough.
A polygon additionally consists of finitely many straight segments. Closure alone supplies neither this regularity nor a nonzero degree.

result.name: A quantitative polygonal replacement theorem
result.statement: The interpolationH(s,t)=(1−s)γ(t)+sp(t) is a homotopy of closed curves avoiding zero, soγ andp have equal winding. Every continuous nonvanishing loop admits such a polygonal approximation.
result.proof: The reverse triangle inequality gives|H(s,t)|≥|γ(t)|−s|p(t)−γ(t)|>d−d=0. Endpoints agree for every intermediate curve becauseγ andp are both closed. Homotopy invariance of degree gives equal winding. For existence, uniform continuity provides a partition fine enough thatγ changes by less thanε<d/2 on each subinterval. Linear interpolation between successive sample values then stays within2ε ofγ there; choosing a smallerε gives the required strict bound. This proof explains why polygonal approximation preserves a topological invariant only with a separation margin from the excluded point.

example.setup: Compare the unit circle, the constant loopγ≡1 and the triangle joining the cube roots of unity.

example.conclusion: Strings, loops and polygons are now distinguished by precise properties rather than by an assumed progression from closure to a particular shape.

entries.title: Boundary conditions are part of a spectral problem
entries.status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
entries.summary: A differential expression alone does not specify an operator. The same second derivative has different spectra under Dirichlet and periodic domains, illustrating the domain gap in a proposed zeta Hamiltonian without pretending to resolve it.
definitions: OnL²(0,π), use the expression−u″. The Dirichlet domain isH²∩H₀¹; the periodic domain requiresu(0)=u(π),u′(0)=u′(π).
An eigenpair consists of a nonzero vector in the chosen domain satisfyingAu=λu. Self-adjointness includes equality with the adjoint domain, not merely a symmetric formal expression.

result.name: Two domains, two exact spectra
result.statement: The Dirichlet eigenvalues aren² forn≥1, with eigenfunctionssin(nx). The periodic eigenvalues are4n² forn∈Z, including zero, with eigenfunctionse^{2inx}.
result.proof: Integration by parts gives〈u,−v″〉−〈−u″,v〉=[u′ conjugate(v)−u conjugate(v′)]₀^π, with the precise conjugation placement adjusted to the inner-product convention. Either stated domain kills this boundary form. Solving−u″=λu gives trigonometric solutions forλ>0; Dirichlet endpoints force√λ to be a positive integer. Periodicity forces e^{i√λπ}=1, hence√λ=2|n|. The constant solves the periodic zero eigenvalue but is excluded by Dirichlet endpoints. Completeness follows from the classical sine and Fourier bases. These regular self-adjoint realizations demonstrate how domain information enters both the eigenvalue equation and its spectral interpretation.

example.setup: Compare the lowest spectral values and boundary behavior.
example.calculation: Dirichlet has lowest eigenvalue one and no constant mode. Periodic has zero followed by four, with the nonzero frequencies occurring in sine/cosine pairs. The same expression therefore gives a different gap and multiplicity structure. A solution of a formal equation that violates an endpoint condition is not an eigenvector of the specified realization.
example.conclusion: The repaired question asks for the domain, boundary form and completeness argument before interpreting a spectral list.

entries.limits: The Bender–Brody–Müller proposal is a specific research construction, not a generic synonym for pseudo-Hermitian matrices. Its primary paper explicitly makes the self-adjointness argument conditional. This example proves neither that construction nor the Riemann hypothesis.

entries.title: A positive metric can repair a matrix inner product
entries.status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
entries.summary: An explicit similarity gives a positive metric and real spectrum for a triangular matrix. A nontrivial Jordan block cannot have such a metric, so pseudo-Hermitian notation alone is insufficient.
definitions: LetA_s=[[1,s],[0,2]] for reals andS=[[1,s],[0,1]], soA_s=Sdiag(1,2)S⁻¹.
A positive metric is a Hermitian positive-definite matrixη defining〈u,v〉_η=u*ηv. Self-adjointness in this inner product isA*η=ηA.

result.name: Explicit quasi-Hermitian metric and its boundary
result.statement: η_s=[[1,−s],[−s,1+s²]] satisfiesA_s*η_s=η_sA_s and is positive definite. A matrix with a nontrivial Jordan block and real eigenvalue admits no positive metric making it self-adjoint.
result.proof: Setη=(S⁻¹)*S⁻¹. Thenv*ηv=||S⁻¹v||²>0 for nonzerov. SubstitutingA=SDS⁻¹, withD real diagonal, provesA*η=ηA. For the obstruction, a positiveη has a positive square root. The transformed matrixB=η^{1/2}Aη^{−1/2} satisfiesB*=B, hence is unitarily diagonalizable and has real eigenvalues. Similarity then makesA diagonalizable too. Thus a Jordan defect cannot be hidden in a positive change of inner product. ForJ=[[1,1],[0,1]], writing a real symmetricη=[[a,b],[b,c]] givesJᵀη−ηJ=[[0,−a],[a,0]], forcinga=0 and contradicting positivity. The general similarity argument also covers complex Hermitian metrics.

example.calculation: Eigenvectorsv₁=(1,0),v₂=(1,1) have ordinary inner product one. Underη=[[1,−1],[−1,2]], their inner product is zero and both have metric norm one. The eigenvalues remain one and two because a change of inner product changes orthogonality, not the algebraic characteristic polynomial. In ordinary coordinates e^{itA_s} has off-diagonal entry s(e^{2it}−e^{it}). At t=π and s=1 its matrix is [[−1,2],[0,1]], whose Euclidean operator norm is 1+√2, although the evolution has norm one in the η metric. Thus real eigenvalues do not alone control Euclidean transient amplification.
example.conclusion: This is a full finite positive-metric construction with an explicit failure case, rather than a conjectural appeal to spectral reality.

entries.title: A modular Hamiltonian is defined by a state
entries.status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
entries.summary: For a positive density matrix the modular Hamiltonian is−logρ. In a commuting finite model its entropy variation is exact to first order, and the negative second variation quantifies concavity. This is distinct from the weight transformation of a modular form.
definitions: Letρ=diag(p₁,…,p_n) withp_i>0 andΣp_i=1. SetK=−logρ andS(ρ)=−Tr(ρlogρ).
A commuting perturbation isρ(ε)=diag(p_i+εv_i), withΣv_i=0 and positivity for sufficiently smallε.
The word modular in this operator definition does not by itself mean a function transforms underSL₂(Z).

result.name: Entropy first variation and strict concavity
result.statement: S′(0)=Tr(δρK)=−Σv_i logp_i, andS″(0)=−Σv_i²/p_i. The second derivative is strictly negative for every nonzero trace-zero diagonal perturbation.
result.proof: Differentiate−(p_i+εv_i)log(p_i+εv_i). The derivative is−v_i(log(p_i+εv_i)+1). At zero the terms−Σv_i cancel by normalization, giving the first-law identity. Differentiating again gives the negative sum. It is strictly negative unless everyv_i is zero. For a Gibbs stateρ=e^{−βH}/Z, functional calculus givesK=βH+logZ·I, so the trace-zero perturbation law becomesδS=βδ〈H〉 whenβ,H are held fixed in that variation. These are consequences of the stated state and normalization, not a prescription for an arbitrary objectH_mod(R) in a gravitational action.

example.calculation: The entropy derivative is−log3, while the second derivative is−(4/3+4)=−16/3. A perturbation toward the more uneven distribution lowers entropy. The formula requiresp_i>0; at an eigenvalue zero,logρ is unbounded on that eigenspace and the differentiability argument changes.
example.conclusion: The construction provides a real operator and variation theorem while keeping two different uses of modular terminology separate.

entries.limits: This finite commuting derivation does not define a modular gravitational action, renormalized black-hole entropy or a modular Hamiltonian for a quantum field region. Matrix positivity and trace normalization are essential.
entries.extension: For noncommuting perturbations, use the Fréchet derivative oflogρ or its resolvent integral to derive the second variation. State a positive lower spectral bound to obtain quantitative continuity and concavity estimates. For the same diagonal family, relative entropy D(p+εv || p) has zero first derivative and second derivative Σv_i²/p_i. This positive quadratic form is the Fisher metric on trace-zero directions. It is the negative of the entropy Hessian here because the reference distribution is fixed in the relative-entropy expression.

entries.title: Moonshine coefficients are graded dimensions and traces
entries.status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
entries.summary: A graded trace separates dimension from the action of a symmetry. A smallS₃ representation gives a complete exact decomposition, while the familiar moonshine dimensions are retained as representation-theoretic data.
definitions: For a graded representationV=⊕V_n of a finite group, its character series isTr_V(gq^{L₀})=ΣTr(g|V_n)qⁿ, formally when every graded piece is finite.
Atg=1 the coefficients are dimensions. Away from the identity they are traces, which can differ even for representations of equal dimension.
TheS₃ classes are identity, transpositions and three-cycles, with sizes1,3,2. Its standard character is(2,0,−1).

result.name: An exact tensor-character decomposition
result.statement: For the two-dimensional standard representationW ofS₃, W⊗W≅1⊕sgn⊕W. At the dimension level the first moonshine coefficient satisfies196884=1+196883; the second satisfies21493760=1+196883+21296876.
result.proof: The permutation representation on three coordinates splits into the constant line and the plane with coordinate sum zero. Counting fixed coordinates gives its trace(3,1,0), so subtracting the constant line givesW character(2,0,−1). Tensor traces multiply, makingW⊗W character(4,0,1). Summing the characters of1,sgn andW gives(1,1,1)+(1,−1,1)+(2,0,−1)=(4,0,1). entries.title: A weight filtration need not split canonically
entries.status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
entries.summary: A two-step filtered vector space admits many splittings, none invariant under all filtration-preserving automorphisms. This elementary example identifies the extra choice suppressed by writing a weight filtration as a direct sum.
definitions: LetV=ke₁⊕ke₂,W₀=ke₁,W₁=W₀,W₂=V, with the evident zero and full extensions outside this range.
The associated graded isGr⁰_W=ke₁ andGr²_W=V/ke₁. A splitting selects a lift of each quotient vector and identifiesV with their direct sum.
A canonical splitting would have to be preserved by every automorphism of the given filtered object.

result.name: No functorial splitting for this filtered object
result.statement: Every complement ofW₀ has the formk(e₂+ce₁). The filtered automorphismsT_a(e₁)=e₁,T_a(e₂)=e₂+ae₁ act transitively on these complements. No complement is fixed by allT_a.
result.proof: A line complementary toke₁ has a vector with nonzeroe₂ coordinate; rescaling it gives e₂+ce₁, proving the classification. ApplyingT_a sends this line to the line with parameterc+a. Choosing any nonzeroa changes it, so no complement can be invariant under the whole automorphism group. EachT_a induces the identity on both graded quotients, showing that the associated graded forgets genuine extension automorphisms. The equality of graded dimensions withdimV therefore does not provide a distinguished decomposition. In mixed Hodge theory additional structures constrain the extensions, and certain splittings may exist after changing scalars or adding hypotheses; those theorems must be stated rather than replacingW_k by an unexplained Hodge-index sum.

example.setup: Compare the complementske₂ andk(e₂+3e₁).
example.calculation: Both project isomorphically toGr²_W and yield identical graded dimensions(1,1). T₃ exchanges the first with the second while acting trivially onGr_W. A numerical routine that returns one complement has selected coordinates, not found an invariant hidden direct-sum decomposition.
example.conclusion: The finite calculation explains exactly why filtrations and decompositions encode different information.

entries.limits: This is a filtered-vector-space theorem, not a classification of mixed Hodge extensions. A pure Hodge decomposition is a different structure and can be canonical under its own hypotheses. The historical formulaW_k=⊕_{p+q=k}H_M^{p,q} conflates indices unless its objects are redefined.
entries.extension: Add a specified nondegenerate inner product and take the orthogonal complement. Then identify the smaller symmetry group preserving that metric and show the splitting is natural only for that smaller category. This exposes the cost of the additional choice.

entries.title: Localization gives a valid motivic and cohomological subtraction
entries.status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
entries.summary: The projective line minus two points gives a fully specified localization example. It has classL−1 and compactly supported cohomology in degrees one and two; no undefined infinite motivic series is needed.
definitions: In the Grothendieck ring of varieties,[X]=[Z]+[X∖Z] for a closed subvarietyZ. SetL=[A¹].
LetX=P¹_C,Z={0,∞},U=C*. The open/closed trianglej_!k_U→k_X→i_*k_Z produces a long exact compact-support cohomology sequence.
The existence of this sheaf-theoretic localization sequence is standard background; its maps and dimensions are computed below.

result.name: Exact class and compact-support cohomology ofC*
result.statement: [C*]=L−1. Over a fieldk,H_c¹(C*;k)=k,H_c²(C*;k)=k and the other compact-support groups vanish. Its compact-support Euler characteristic is zero.
result.proof: DecomposeP¹ intoA¹ and the point at infinity to obtain[P¹]=L+1. Removing two points givesL−1. In the long exact sequence, H⁰(P¹)=k maps toH⁰(Z)=k² by the diagonal mapc↦(c,c). Its kernel is zero and cokernel is one-dimensional, soH_c⁰(U)=0 andH_c¹(U)=k. SinceH¹(P¹)=0,H¹(Z)=0,H²(P¹)=k andH²(Z)=0, exactness givesH_c²(U)=k. Hence the Euler characteristic is−1+1=0. The cohomological subtraction includes connecting maps and degrees; it is not literal subtraction of ordinary vector spaces. Its numerical Euler realization agrees with evaluatingL at one in the classL−1.

example.calculation: The column(1,1)ᵀ has rank one. The quotientk²/diag(k) is detected by(a,b)↦b−a. Thus two removed points create one compact-support degree-one class, even thoughC* itself has no compact connected component.
example.conclusion: This is a constructive interpretation of additivity, six-operation notation and a motivic class in one exact example.

entries.limits: A motivic integral over arcs additionally needs a measure, cylinder normalization and a completed coefficient ring. The recovered sumΣ[X_n]L^−n does not automatically converge or define that measure. No quantum volume is inferred.

entries.summary: Projecting the standard240 E₈roots onto their first four coordinates gives the48 F₄root vectors with unequal multiplicities, together with zero. The24 long projected roots formD₄, but the entire image is larger.

entries.title: A Jacobiator detects nonassociativity only after multiplication is defined
entries.status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
entries.summary: Associative commutators satisfy Jacobi by cancellation. An explicit octonion triple has a nonzero Jacobiator, furnishing a concrete nonassociative example without identifying it with a physicalR-flux.
definitions: For a bilinear multiplication define[a,b]=ab−ba andJ(a,b,c)=[a,[b,c]]+[b,[c,a]]+[c,[a,b]].
Use octonion unitse₁,…,e₇ with squares−1 and oriented Fano triples(123),(145),(176),(246),(257),(347),(365); reversing an ordered pair changes sign.
The associator is(a,b,c)=(ab)c−a(bc). Parentheses cannot be omitted in a nonassociative product.

result.name: An exact nonzero Jacobiator
result.statement: For(a,b,c)=(e₁,e₂,e₄), the associator is2e₇ andJ=−12e₇. In every associative algebra the same commutator formula hasJ=0.
result.proof: In an associative algebra expand the three nested commutators. Each of the six ordered triple products occurs twice with opposite signs, giving zero. In the specified octonion table,e₂e₄=e₆,e₁e₆=−e₇, so[e₁,[e₂,e₄]]=−4e₇. Alsoe₄e₁=−e₅,e₂e₅=e₇, giving the second term−4e₇. Finallye₁e₂=e₃,e₄e₃=−e₇ gives the third−4e₇. Their sum is−12e₇. Separately(e₁e₂)e₄=e₃e₄=e₇, wherease₁(e₂e₄)=e₁e₆=−e₇, giving associator2e₇. This verifies the sign convention rather than appealing to a generic nonassociative slogan. Left multiplication still represents every octonion as a linear map, but it is not a product-preserving representation: L_{e₁}L_{e₂}e₄=−e₇ whereas L_{e₁e₂}e₄=e₇. Commutators of the linear maps satisfy Jacobi, while the octonion commutators need not. This prevents confusing an operator embedding with an associative algebra embedding.

example.setup: Compare this triple with the quaternionic subalgebra spanned by1,e₁,e₂,e₃.
example.calculation: Within that four-dimensional subalgebra multiplication is associative and every commutator Jacobiator vanishes. The chosen triple involvinge₄ leaves that subalgebra and gives the nonzero value above. Thus a large algebra can contain associative sectors without being associative globally.
example.conclusion: A nonzero Jacobiator is now attached to a declared multiplication table and a checked triple.

entries.limits: Ordinary bounded matrices cannot realize this multiplication associatively while preserving all products, since their commutators always satisfy Jacobi. entries.summary: A finite nonnegative input network has a convergent response series when its spectral radius is below one. A two-sector example yields an exact multiplier, showing why a universal scalar such as2.68 needs a declared model.
definitions: Letx=Ax+d, whereA has nonnegative entries andd is an external input. All coordinates use compatible units.

result.statement: ForA=[[0,1/4],[1/2,0]],(I−A)⁻¹=[[8/7,2/7],[4/7,8/7]]. A unit shock in sector one gives total output12/7; a unit shock in sector two gives10/7.

entries.title: Weighted scores and capacity quotas need different constraints
entries.status: Developed mathematical result with explicit hypotheses and checked example; historical claims repaired where necessary
entries.summary: A quotient of capacity by demand is not itself an allocation theorem. A concave two-recipient model yields a unique feasible optimum and an exact water-filling rule.
definitions: Letx_i≥0 be allocated units withΣx_i≤C,C>0. Let benefit beΣa_i log(1+x_i), witha_i>0.

result.statement: The log-utility problem has a unique optimumx_i=max(a_i/λ−1,0), withλ>0 chosen soΣx_i=C. For(a₁,a₂)=(2,1),C=2, the allocation is(5/3,1/3).
result.proof: The compact feasible simplex gives existence. The Hessian is diagonal with strictly negative entries−a_i/(1+x_i)², so the objective is strictly concave and has at most one maximizer. Each benefit increases, so capacity is exhausted. Lagrange optimality givesa_i/(1+x_i)=λ on positive coordinates and a_i≤λ on zero coordinates. These conditions yield the formula and are sufficient by concavity. For the example both coordinates are positive, so2/λ−1+1/λ−1=2 givesλ=3/4 and the displayed allocation.

Concentration at(2,0) has first marginal2/3 and second marginal one, so it is also improvable. The certificate uses exact marginal comparisons rather than promotional ranking.
example.conclusion: A feasible allocation and an aggregate index have explicit but different mathematical contracts.

definitions: LetD_{t+1}=(1+r)D_t+P_t andY_{t+1}=(1+g)Y_t withg>−1. Writeb_t=D_t/Y_t andp_t=P_t/Y_t.

entries.summary: A constant-potential equation on a periodic parameter has a complete monodromy calculation. The zero-potential case has only eigenvalue one but a nonidentity Jordan block, exposing a condition that spectral eigenvalues alone miss.

entries.status: Developed mathematical repair or classical result; speculative source claims delimited
entries.summary: The external topic label combines a wavelet with curl-flux integrals and proposed topological invariants. A precise first step is Stokes’ theorem. definitions: Let S be a compact oriented piecewise smooth surface in R³ with oriented boundary C. Let F be C¹ on a neighborhood of S.
Define Φ_F(S)=∫_S(curl F)·n dA. Boundary orientation is chosen by the usual right-hand convention. For a closed surface assume the additional smoothness needed for the divergence theorem.

result.name: Stokes independence with fixed boundary, and a counterexample to topological invariance
result.statement: Φ_F(S)=∮_C F·dr. Consequently two admissible surfaces with the same oriented boundary give the same integral for the same field. The value can nevertheless vary continuously under changes of F while the surface topology stays fixed.
result.proof: Stokes’ theorem is the explicit classical input identifying the surface integral with circulation. Applying it to S₁ and S₂ with the same C gives equal values, provided F is defined smoothly on both. For a closed surface bounding a region with a smooth field, divergence of curl is zero, so its flux is zero; this also follows from Stokes because the boundary is empty. To show that no nontrivial topological invariant follows merely from the integral, use F_a(x,y,z)=a(−y,x,0)/2. Its curl is (0,0,a). On the unit disk in the xy-plane the flux is aπ, which ranges over all real values as a changes. The disk’s topology has not changed. The equality with circulation still holds, so the failure is in the proposed interpretation rather than in Stokes’ theorem.

example.calculation: The curl is (0,0,1), so the flux is the area 4π. Parameterize its boundary by r(t)=(2cos t,2sin t,0). entries.status: Developed mathematical repair or classical result; speculative source claims delimited
entries.summary: Rational approximation and nonlinear iteration were named in the adaptive framework, but the retrieved exponential approximation bound is truncated. Two modest exact statements replace that missing certificate: a spectral maximum bound and a local Newton remainder estimate. Neither relies on an unrecorded Zolotarev constant.
definitions: Let A be real symmetric with spectrum in [a,b]. Let r be a rational function with no pole on that interval and f continuous there.
For Newton’s method let F be C² near a root α, assume |F′|≥m>0 and |F″|≤M on an interval containing α and the current iterate, and assume the next iterates remain in that interval.

result.name: Spectral error transfer and a local quadratic recurrence
result.statement: ||f(A)−r(A)||₂=max_{λ∈spectrum(A)}|f(λ)−r(λ)|≤sup_[a,b]|f−r|. Newton’s update x⁺=x−F(x)/F′(x) satisfies |x⁺−α|≤[M/(2m)]|x−α|² under the stated local bounds.
result.proof: An orthogonal diagonalization A=Udiag(λ_i)Uᵀ makes f(A)−r(A) orthogonally similar to the diagonal matrix of scalar errors; its Euclidean operator norm is the largest absolute diagonal entry. The pole exclusion makes r(A) well defined. For Newton, Taylor-expand F(α)=F(x)+F′(x)(α−x)+F″(ξ)(α−x)²/2 for some intermediate ξ. Rearranging and using F(α)=0 gives x⁺−α=F″(ξ)(x−α)²/[2F′(x)], up to an irrelevant sign, proving the absolute bound. Remaining inside the interval is a real hypothesis: a local error estimate is not global convergence from every initial point.

example.setup: Use A=diag(1,2), f(λ)=1/λ and r(λ)=3/2−λ/2. Separately use F(x)=x²−2 and x₀=3/2.
example.calculation: The polynomial r is exact at both eigenvalues, so r(A)=A^(−1), although it is not exact throughout [1,2]. Newton gives x₁=17/12 and x₂=577/408. The exact residuals are x₁²−2=1/144 and x₂²−2=1/166464. These are also Pell-type rational certificates, computed without floating-point cancellation.
example.conclusion: A finite spectrum can make a simple approximation exact, while iteration convergence requires a separate nonlinear argument.

entries.limits: No unrecovered uniform rational-approximation rate, prime-grid optimization complexity or arbitrary-start Newton guarantee is asserted. A residual-to-error bound additionally needs a derivative or inverse-conditioning estimate.
entries.extension: For a prescribed positive interval [a,b], optimize a pole-free rational approximation and certify its scalar uniform error. That certificate then transfers immediately to every symmetric matrix with spectrum in the interval, independently of dimension.

entries.title: Tripartite information vanishes for every pure three-party state
entries.status: Developed mathematical repair or classical result; speculative source claims delimited
entries.summary: The source’s GHZ endpoint is consistent, but a slightly negative tripartite-information caveat for a pure W endpoint is not. For a pure state of exactly three parties, the quantity vanishes identically. This is a structural obstruction to using it as the proposed transition marker, independent of numerical precision.
definitions: For a density matrix ρ define S(ρ)=−tr(ρlog₂ρ), with 0log0=0. For a pure state on A⊗B⊗C define I₃=S_A+S_B+S_C−S_AB−S_AC−S_BC+S_ABC.
GHZ=(|000⟩+|111⟩)/√2 and W=(|001⟩+|010⟩+|100⟩)/√3. The retrieved parameterized state ψ(g) was not supplied.

result.name: Pure-state cancellation and unequal entanglement spectra
result.statement: Every finite-dimensional pure three-party state has I₃=0. GHZ has all nontrivial one-party and two-party entropies equal to one; W has them equal to h₂(1/3)≈0.9182958341. The two states therefore share I₃ despite different reduced spectra.
result.proof: The Schmidt decomposition across A versus BC gives identical nonzero eigenvalues for ρ_A and ρ_BC, so S_A=S_BC. The other two bipartitions give S_B=S_AC and S_C=S_AB. Purity gives S_ABC=0. Substituting cancels every term. For GHZ, tracing two qubits leaves diag(1/2,1/2). For W it leaves diag(2/3,1/3); permutation symmetry makes this true for each party. The two-party entropies follow from the same Schmidt argument, avoiding a larger eigenproblem. This proves exact zero rather than an approximately small or slightly negative value.

example.setup: As a declared new comparison family take ψ(θ)=cosθ|000⟩+sinθ|111⟩ for 0≤θ≤π/2.
example.calculation: Every one-party entropy is h₂(sin²θ), every two-party entropy is the same, and I₃=0 throughout. At θ=0 it is a product; at θ=π/4 it is GHZ. The entropy changes continuously, while I₃ contains no information about this change. The verifier checks the reduced diagonal eigenvalues for GHZ/W and the exact entropy cancellations numerically.
example.conclusion: A vanishing summary statistic does not imply absent entanglement and cannot locate the claimed g=1 or1.67 transitions without a specified state and observable.

entries.limits: Mixed three-party states can have nonzero I₃, and a subsystem of a larger pure system is generally mixed. The theorem is for a globally pure state of exactly A,B,C. No historical ψ(g) is reconstructed from endpoint labels.
entries.extension: Specify a full normalized state family and compare reduced-spectrum invariants, genuine multipartite entanglement measures and filtration changes separately. Any proposed transition must be defined before numerical thresholds are tested.

entries.summary: The historical state, weights and filtration were not recovered, so its claimed transition parameters cannot be recomputed. A completely declared triangle filtration nevertheless demonstrates the exact distinction needed: positive weights change eigenvalues, whereas adding a filling simplex can change homology. This is a new mathematical example, not an inferred ψ(g).
definitions: Orient triangle edges 01,12,20 and use boundary B₁=[[-1,0,1],[1,−1,0],[0,1,−1]]. Without a face, B₂ is absent; with a face its boundary column is (1,1,1)ᵀ.
Use the unweighted edge Hodge Laplacian Δ₁=B₁ᵀB₁+B₂B₂ᵀ. A filtration is an increasing sequence of simplicial complexes, including all faces of every entered simplex.

result.name: The harmonic edge disappears exactly when the face is added
result.statement: For the unfilled triangle, Δ₁ has eigenvalues 0,3,3 with harmonic vector (1,1,1). After adding the face, Δ₁=3I and its kernel is zero. This matches β₁=1 and β₁=0 respectively.
result.proof: The boundary sum B₁(1,1,1)ᵀ is zero, so B₁B₂=0 and the complex is valid. Direct multiplication gives B₁ᵀB₁=3I−J, where J has every entry one. J has eigenvalue three on constants and zero on their orthogonal complement, producing the unfilled spectrum. Adding B₂B₂ᵀ=J yields 3I. More generally xᵀΔ₁x=||B₁x||²+||B₂ᵀx||²; therefore its kernel consists of cycles orthogonal to boundaries and represents homology in this finite inner-product model. Replacing the inner products by positive definite weights preserves the dimension of that harmonic space; positive weights do not by themselves create a new simplex or a new homology class.

example.setup: Let all edges enter at threshold zero and the face enter at threshold two.
example.calculation: The degree-one persistence interval begins at zero and ends at two. Before two there is one independent edge cycle; afterwards it is the boundary of the new face. A weighted eigenvalue crossing zero caused only by a weight becoming singular would instead leave the positive-definite setting and requires a different explanation. The verifier checks both spectra through exact matrix identities and ranks.

entries.title: Derived tensor products record information an ordinary product erases
entries.status: Developed mathematical repair or classical result; speculative source claims delimited
entries.summary: The recovered manuscript description lists derived objects but supplies no defining equations. A small algebraic example shows exactly why deriving a functor can matter. It is deliberately an authored comparison, not a claimed construction of the absent stacks, sheaves or path integrals.
definitions: Let k be a field, A=k[ε]/(ε²), and regard k=A/(ε) as an A-module. Ordinary tensor gives k⊗_Ak≅k.
Tor_n^A(k,k) is the nth homology of a free resolution of one copy of k after tensoring with the other. The derived tensor k⊗_A^Lk retains this whole homology sequence.

result.name: An explicit resolution with a higher class in every degree
result.statement: For every n≥0, Tor_n^A(k,k)≅k. Thus the derived tensor cannot be replaced by its degree-zero ordinary tensor without losing nonzero information in every positive degree.
result.proof: Use the augmented complex …→A→A→A→k→0, with every positive-degree differential multiplication by ε and the final map the quotient. Consecutive differentials compose to multiplication by ε²=0. In A, an element is a+bε; multiplying by ε gives aε, so the kernel and image of multiplication by ε are both the one-dimensional ideal εA. The kernel of A→k is also εA. Hence the complex is an exact free resolution. Tensoring with k sends ε to zero, so all resulting differentials vanish and each chain group is k. Its homology is therefore k in every nonnegative degree. This is a complete calculation rather than an invocation of derived language alone.

example.setup: Represent multiplication by ε on the basis (1,ε) as M=[[0,0],[1,0]].
example.calculation: Then M²=0, rank(M)=1 and kernel(M)=span(ε)=image(M). Reducing coefficients modulo ε turns M into zero on the tensor complex. The verifier checks these finite linear identities and the first eight homology dimensions. The written periodic argument proves the all-degree statement.
example.conclusion: Higher Tor is the information that ordinary tensor discards; a derived replacement must be justified by such an actual failure of exactness.

entries.limits: This is a module calculation over dual numbers, not a motivic cohomology computation, an E∞ structure or a syntomic integration measure. Passing from complexes to those theories requires their own objects, maps and comparison theorems.
entries.extension: Build a small verified chain-complex library that certifies d²=0, exactness and chain-homotopy equivalence. Only then add a geometric input functor and ask which derived invariants it computes, with explicit test objects and coefficient rings.

entries.status: Developed mathematical repair or classical result; speculative source claims delimited
entries.summary: A valuation map has a precise and useful loss of information. Its tropical balancing condition follows from the nonarchimedean triangle inequality, but it does not determine the original coordinates or a reconstruction advantage. definitions: Let K be a nonarchimedean valued field with additive valuation v, so v(xy)=v(x)+v(y) and v(x+y)≥min(v(x),v(y)). Set v(0)=∞.
For nonzero x,y on X={x+y+1=0}, define trop(x,y)=(u,w)=(v(x),v(y)). Use the minimum convention.

result.name: A tropical line and a strict information-loss example
result.statement: Every such point satisfies that min(u,w,0) is attained at least twice. Its possible finite valuation pattern lies on the three rays (u,0) with u≥0, (0,w) with w≥0, or (u,u) with u≤0. Valuations alone do not test an individual proposed lift.
result.proof: If one of three nonzero summands has strictly smaller valuation than the other two, the sum of the other two has larger valuation and cannot cancel it. Therefore x+y+1=0 forces a repeated minimum. Enumerating which two entries attain it gives the three rays. Conversely, interpreting the rays as the complete tropical variety requires a lifting theorem over a suitable valued algebraic closure; only the elementary necessary condition is used here. The loss of unit data is concrete: over Q₃, (x,y)=(1,−2) lies on X and has valuations (0,0), while (1,1) has the same valuations but gives x+y+1=3≠0. Thus one valuation pair supports both an actual solution and a nonsolution depending on the leading units.

example.setup: Compare Q₃ points (1,−2), (3,−4) and the proposed pair (1,1).
example.calculation: The first has valuation (0,0), the second (1,0); each has a repeated minimum and exactly satisfies the equation. The third has the same tropical coordinates as the first but fails the original equation. Multiplication also illustrates retained structure: v₃(3·(−4))=1+0=1. These exact integer valuations are checked without a p-adic numerical library.

entries.title: A p-adic integral can be evaluated exactly by valuation shells
entries.status: Developed mathematical repair or classical result; speculative source claims delimited
entries.summary: The source names an integral over p-adic integer points, but an integrand, measure and convergence claim still have to be specified. The monomial case supplies a complete local-zeta calculation: its rationality comes from a geometric series rather than from a speculative decoding interpretation.
definitions: Fix a prime p and normalize Haar measure μ(Z_p)=1. Then μ(p^nZ_p)=p^(−n), and |x|_p=p^(−v_p(x)) for x≠0.
For complex s define |x|_p^s=exp(s log|x|_p). The singleton zero has measure zero and may be assigned any value when the integral is finite.

result.name: An exact local zeta integral
result.statement: For Re(s)>−1, Z_p(s)=∫_{Z_p}|x|_p^s dμ=(1−p^(−1))/(1−p^(−s−1)). The integral is absolutely convergent exactly in this half-plane; the displayed rational-in-p^(−s) expression also supplies a meromorphic continuation.
result.proof: Partition nonzero Z_p into shells A_n=p^nZ_p∖p^(n+1)Z_p, n≥0. Their measures are (1−p^(−1))p^(−n), and the integrand is constant p^(−ns) on each shell. Thus Z_p(s)=(1−p^(−1))Σ_{n≥0}p^(−n(s+1)). Absolute convergence is equivalent to |p^(−s−1)|<1, or Re(s)>−1, and summation gives the formula. If Re(s)≤−1, the positive integral of the absolute value diverges by the same series. Analytic continuation is a statement about the resulting function; it does not make the original divergent integral convergent outside its initial half-plane.

example.setup: Choose p=3 and s=2, then compare shell integration with a finite residue approximation.
example.calculation: The exact answer is (2/3)/(1−1/27)=9/13. The first N shells sum to (9/13)(1−27^(−N)), with omitted tail (9/13)27^(−N). In a residue calculation modulo 3^N, each congruence class has measure 3^(−N); valuations below N reproduce those shell counts exactly. The unresolved zero class contributes a bounded tail rather than an arbitrary replacement value.
example.conclusion: The calculation includes its normalization, domain and an exact truncation error, making it suitable for a reproducible arithmetic implementation.

entries.limits: A general variety X(Z_p), singular polynomial or oscillatory integrand needs additional geometry and convergence hypotheses. This one-variable proof is not a proof of the full rationality theory or of a physical detector.
entries.extension: For a polynomial f, count solutions f(x)≡0 modulo p^N and relate those counts to the measure of valuation sublevel sets. A proved resolution or cell decomposition can then replace the elementary shell structure used here.

definitions: For a stipulated system boundary let E_out≥0 be useful returned energy and E_in>0 invested energy in the same units and time horizon. Define R=E_out/E_in.

result.statement: An output of11923kWh with ratio28.6 requires an invested denominator11923/28.6≈416.8881119kWh. The output alone does not determine EROI. entries.summary: A fitted score and a theorem about unseen samples are different mathematical objects. The source’s spectral PAC–Bayes claim does not provide its prior, posterior, sample law or loss bound. A standard finite-hypothesis theorem can be derived transparently and shows exactly where those assumptions enter.
definitions: Let H be finite, P a strictly positive prior fixed independently of an iid sample of size m, and ℓ(h,z)∈[0,1]. Define population loss L(h), empirical loss Lhat(h), and KL(Q||P)=ΣQ(h)log[Q(h)/P(h)].
Fix λ>0 andδ∈(0,1) before seeing the sample. Write L(Q),Lhat(Q) for posterior averages.

result.name: A fixed-parameter PAC–Bayes–Hoeffding bound
result.statement: With probability at least1−δ, simultaneously for every posterior Q, L(Q)≤Lhat(Q)+[KL(Q||P)+log(1/δ)]/λ+λ/(8m). This is a theorem under the declared iid bounded-loss model, not a consequence of R² or a spectral fit.
result.proof: Hoeffding’s bounded-variable lemma gives E_sample exp(λ[L(h)−Lhat(h)])≤exp(λ²/(8m)) for each h. Average over the fixed prior and apply Markov: with probability at least1−δ, log E_P exp(λ[L−Lhat])≤λ²/(8m)+log(1/δ). For any finite probability Q, Jensen’s inequality applied after writing the prior sum using Q gives λE_Q(L−Lhat)≤KL(Q||P)+log E_P exp(λ[L−Lhat]). Combining proves the bound uniformly in Q on that one event. Zero posterior masses are handled by continuity. Optimizing λ after observing Q requires a separate uniformization or parameter grid; the fixed-λ theorem does not silently supply it.

example.setup: Choose two hypotheses with uniform prior, a point-mass posterior, m=100,δ=.05,λ=20 and empirical loss.1.
example.calculation: Then KL=log2 and the penalty is log40/20+20/800≈.2094439727, giving L(Q)≤.3094439727 on the stated event. Separately R²=1−SSE/SST only describes squared errors on its evaluated response set; the number.847 omits the response normalization, split and dependency assumptions needed to connect it with this theorem.
example.conclusion: The proof makes its probability event, optimization domain and constants reviewable, while preserving the empirical report as a claim rather than a verified forecast.

entries.limits: Prime-indexed observations are not automatically iid. Unbounded squared loss is outside the bounded-loss theorem unless explicitly controlled. A data-dependent prior needs another theorem. No cryptographic or cross-domain benefit follows from this certificate.
entries.extension: Specify a dependency model, bounded or tail-controlled loss and a prior independent of the held-out data. A spectral hypothesis can enter only through a proved complexity or KL estimate, after which the actual numerical bound should be reported alongside the score.

entries.title: Multiplicative convolution has a precise divisor algebra
entries.status: Developed mathematical repair or classical result; speculative source claims delimited
entries.summary: The historical report’s multiplicative-function approximation and inversion claims lack their actual kernel and norms. The classical divisor convolution gives a well-defined replacement. It proves an exact transform product when absolute convergence permits regrouping, rather than asserting a universal approximation capability.
definitions: For arithmetic functions f,g:N→C, define(f*g)(n)=Σ_{d|n}f(d)g(n/d). Let1(n)=1 and ε(1)=1, ε(n)=0 for n>1.
A function is multiplicative if f(mn)=f(m)f(n) for coprime m,n and f(1)=1. Its Dirichlet series is D_f(s)=Σf(n)n^(−s) where absolutely convergent.

result.name: Convolution, inversion and a transform product
result.statement: Dirichlet convolution is associative and commutative with identity ε. The Möbius function satisfies μ*1=ε. Whenever D_f,D_g converge absolutely, D_(f*g)(s)=D_f(s)D_g(s). Multiplicative inputs give a multiplicative convolution.
result.proof: Associativity follows by writing either parenthesization as the finite sum overabc=n of f(a)g(b)h(c); commutativity swaps complementary divisors. For μ, summing μ(d) over divisors of n factors as∏_{p|n}(1−1), zero unless n=1. The Dirichlet-series product is the absolutely convergent double sumΣ_{a,b}f(a)g(b)(ab)^(−s); group terms by n=ab to obtain the formula. For coprime m,n, each divisor of mn decomposes uniquely into a divisor of m times a divisor of n, so the convolution sum factors. These are concrete algebraic and analytic hypotheses, not consequences of a neural architecture name.

example.setup: Take f=g=1, then invert the divisor-count function τ=1*1 by μ.
example.calculation: τ(12)=6 from divisors1,2,3,4,6,12. The identity μ*τ=1 gives at12 the sum τ(12)−τ(6)−τ(4)+τ(2)=6−4−3+2=1. Consequently the absolutely convergent series of τ is ζ(s)² for Re(s)>1. The verifier checks the convolution and inversion on every integer through120.
example.conclusion: A finite implementation can certify these exact arithmetic identities while leaving approximation and extrapolation claims separate.

entries.limits: This does not prove exponential approximation of arbitrary multiplicative functions, inversion of a noisy learned transform, or a number-theoretic theorem from finite training. Other notions of multiplicative convolution, such as Haar convolution on R_+, need different definitions.
entries.extension: For a specified truncated divisor transform, compute its triangular matrix and exact inverse. Then derive a perturbation norm bound for noisy coefficients, making conditioning and truncation error explicit before claiming stable inversion.

entries.status: Developed mathematical repair or classical result; speculative source claims delimited
entries.summary: The late-month source includes a heat-flux formula with A/V where conservation requires V/A. A short energy balance fixes that inversion. definitions: For a uniform thermal capacity C=ρc_pV, a permitted temperature rise ΔT stores energy CΔT. Let A be the area receiving a uniform flux q″ for duration t_p.
For a stated lumped linear model, τTdot+T=T_input after normalizing the temperature deviation. A unit step starting from zero gives T(t)=1−e^(−t/τ).

result.name: Energy-limited flux and a certified short-pulse response
result.statement: Ignoring heat losses, q″≤ρc_pΔT(V/A)/t_p is necessary to keep the stored-energy rise within CΔT. The source’s factor(A/V) has the wrong length dimension. With τ=.8s and t_p=.0002s, the step fraction is1−e^(−1/4000)≈.000249968753.
result.proof: Incoming energy is q″At_p. Requiring it to be no more thanρc_pVΔT and dividing by positive At_p gives the bound. The units are[J/(m³K)]·K·m/s=W/m²; replacing V/A by A/V would instead give W/m⁴. For the response, solve τTdot+T=1 by an integrating factor to obtain1−e^(−t/τ). For0≤x≤1, integrating1−u≤e^(−u)≤1 from zero to x gives x−x²/2≤1−e^(−x)≤x. Taking x=1/4000 encloses the response between.00024996875 and.00025. This is a rigorous bound in the declared first-order model.

example.calculation: Stored capacity is24 energy units and the allowed uniform flux is24/(6·2)=2. The source’s inverted geometry would produce8, four times larger in this example and with inconsistent dimensions. Separately τ/t_p=4000 for the retrieved time scales, so a full response within one pulse is not supplied by this single-state step model.

entries.title: A bonded-layer stress calculation needs a compatibility model
entries.status: Developed mathematical repair or classical result; speculative source claims delimited
entries.summary: A stress value is not determined by thermal expansion coefficients alone. A simple bonded-bar model states its mechanical assumptions and produces an exact stress formula by energy minimization. It is an illustrative calculation rather than validation of the reported274.5MPa or an operational limit.
definitions: Two perfectly bonded axial layers share strainε and temperature changeΔT. Their areas are A_i>0, moduli E_i>0 and expansion coefficientsα_i. Assume no net external axial force, no bending and linear elasticity.
Their stresses areσ_i=E_i(ε−α_iΔT), and stored elastic energy per common length is U(ε)=ΣA_iE_i(ε−α_iΔT)²/2.

result.name: Compatible strain as a unique convex minimizer
result.statement: The common strain isε*=ΔT(ΣA_iE_iα_i)/(ΣA_iE_i), withΣA_iσ_i=0. For equal A and E, stresses are±E(α₂−α₁)ΔT/2. Changing boundary constraints changes the result.
result.proof: Differentiate U to obtain U′=ΣA_iE_i(ε−α_iΔT). Setting this to zero is exactly axial force balance. Since U″=ΣA_iE_i>0, the stationary point is the unique global minimizer. Substitution yields the strain formula and equal-layer stresses. If both layers were externally constrained toε=0, the stresses would instead be−E_iα_iΔT, showing why omitted compatibility data cannot be repaired by a more precise multiplication. The stress dimensions are modulus times dimensionless strain; expansion coefficients carry inverse-temperature units.

example.setup: Choose a declared model with equal layers, E=200GPa,α₂−α₁=10^(−5)K^(−1) andΔT=100K.
example.calculation: The stress magnitudes are100MPa, opposite in sign. The result is exact for these stipulated decimals. Separately the source’s specific-mass figures7.48 and6.8kg/kW differ by exactly10% relative to6.8; without the mass and power denominator neither is established. A reported electrophoretic velocity likewise cannot be recomputed without its field and mobility model.
example.conclusion: The example supplies a practical compatibility certificate and identifies which historical numbers lack sufficient inputs.

entries.limits: Actual multilayers can bend, relax, creep, delaminate or have nonuniform temperature. The bar model is not an interface-failure criterion or a substitute for measurements. No strength, flight or deposition recommendation follows.
entries.extension: For a specified laminate, minimize a quadratic energy over midplane strain and curvature and propagate interval material parameters to stress bounds. Compare those bounds with independently measured strength distributions rather than treating one nominal stress as a reliability probability.

entries.title: Effective conductivity depends on geometry and interface resistance
entries.status: Developed mathematical repair or classical result; speculative source claims delimited
entries.summary: Practical vector calculus is enough to expose the missing geometry. Parallel layers and series layers made from identical fractions have different exact effective conductivities. An interface resistance adds another independent parameter, so neither a nominal filler percentage nor a single multiplication validates the reported heat flux.
definitions: Use Fourier’s law q=−κ∇T withκ>0. On a stationary one-dimensional layered sample, constant flux and temperature drops determine its effective conductivity.
Let fractions f and1−f have conductivitiesκ₂ andκ₁. Parallel paths share a gradient; series layers share a flux. An interface resistance R_c≥0 gives temperature jump R_cq″.

result.name: Two exact effective-conductivity formulas and a conservation identity
result.statement: Parallel geometry givesκ_parallel=(1−f)κ₁+fκ₂; series geometry givesκ_series=[(1−f)/κ₁+f/κ₂]^(−1). For total thicknessℓ, contact resistance changes the series value toκ_eff=ℓ/[ℓ₁/κ₁+ℓ₂/κ₂+R_c]. Heat conservation isρc_pT_t=−div q+s.
result.proof: In parallel, sum area-weighted fluxes−κ_i∇T; the common gradient factors out. In series, each layer drops q″ℓ_i/κ_i, so the total drop is q″Σℓ_i/κ_i. Defining q″=κ_effΔT/ℓ yields the harmonic formula and the contact version after adding the jump. The arithmetic value exceeds the harmonic one by the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality applied to positive weighted conductivities and reciprocals. Conservation follows by equating the rate of stored energy in any control volume with incoming boundary flux plus sources, then applying the divergence theorem. These arguments require no Hodge decomposition or unvalidated learned predictor.

example.setup: Stipulateκ₁=320,f=.12 as retrieved inputs, and chooseκ₂=1 only as a new illustrative contrast.
example.calculation: The parallel value is281.72, while the series value is4000/491≈8.14664 in the same conductivity units. Ifκ₂ were idealized as zero, the parallel limit would be281.6, matching one source number only under that extra idealization; the series limit would instead be zero. The verifier checks the rational formulas and the contact-resistance monotonicity.
example.conclusion: The same fractions support radically different exact values depending on transport geometry, so a reported κ_eff needs a declared model and data.

entries.limits: The illustrativeκ₂ is not a material measurement. Arbitrary microstructures need a homogenization theorem or experiment; anisotropy requires a positive-definite conductivity tensor. Numerical metrics such as96.8% prediction accuracy or±2.8% variation are not validated here.
entries.extension: Pose a periodic conductivity cell problem, solve it with certified energy bounds and compare the resulting tensor against series/parallel limits. Interface resistances and uncertainty intervals should enter the same variational formulation.

result.statement: For(2,6436341,6436343), rad(abc)=15042 and q≈1.6299116841. For(121,109375,109496), the radical is10538990 and q≈.7175768892, not1.5808. The displayed(24833,181307,22784) is not an ABC triple because the first two entries sum to206140.

entries.status: Developed mathematical repair or classical result; speculative source claims delimited
entries.summary: The analyzer names many rapidly growing sequences and exponents. A modular filter can be completely rigorous, but its scope is a particular equation, modulus and range. One simple obstruction already separates even and odd degrees rather than producing a universal threshold at seven.
definitions: For a modulus M≥2 define R_d(M)={x^d mod M:x∈Z/MZ}. If S(n)±k=m^d then its residue must belong to R_d(M).
Take S(n)=n!, k=1, n≥3. For a prime p, the nonzero dth powers form the image of the dth-power map on the cyclic group F_p×.

result.name: An all-n factorial exclusion and an exact residue count
result.statement: For every even d≥2 and n≥3, n!−1 is not a dth power of an integer. For a prime p, |R_d(p)|=1+(p−1)/gcd(d,p−1).

entries.status: Developed mathematical repair or classical result; speculative source claims delimited
entries.summary: The source provides a piecewise ratio but not a justified physical interpretation. Its divisibility content is elementary and useful: prime-adic valuations determine exactly which branch applies and give a stable implementation without forming a gigantic factorial.
definitions: For positive integers n,k let g=gcd(k,n!). Defineρ(n,k)=n!/g if k divides n!, andρ(n,k)=g/k otherwise, following the retrieved branch convention.

result.name: Legendre valuations decide the branch exactly
result.statement: g=∏_{p|k}p^{min(a_p,Σfloor(n/p^j))}; k divides n! exactly when each a_p is at most that factorial valuation. In the divisible branchρ=n!/k; otherwiseρ is the reciprocal of the positive integer k/g.
result.proof: Count each factor of p in1,…,n. Multiples of p contribute one, multiples of p² contribute an additional one, and so on, proving Legendre’s sum. If k|n!, then g=k and the first branch simplifies as stated. In the other branch k/g is an integer greater than one, soρ=g/k∈(0,1). entries.status: Developed mathematical repair or classical result; speculative source claims delimited
entries.summary: The interval and numerical setup of the reported eigenvalues were not recovered. A bounded-interval point-interaction model nevertheless supports precise domain, min–max and perturbation statements.
